name: Agile Team Member (ATeM)
one_liner: Cross-disciplinary generalist who builds and tests the information system each iteration.
purpose: The Agile Team Member (ATeM) focuses on producing the actual information system that is part of the project's solution. The role encompasses architecture, analysis, design, programming, testing, planning and estimation, so ATeMs have cross-disciplinary skills even though the degree of specialisation varies from individual to individual. They are generalists, as opposed to traditional highly-specialised roles such as developers, analysts and testers.
meta: Performing layer — core role of the Agile Project Core Team (A-PCT)
Generalists, not specialists: architecture, analysis, design, code, test, planning, estimation

fields.what: Participates in the planning and estimation of iterations and releases, supplying the relative estimates.
fields.pollux: Lamarr, Babbage and Eiffel size the reconciliation work for Release 2.

fields.what: Participates in the solution architecture design rather than receiving it from the Architecture Owner.
fields.pollux: The three ATeMs shape the data model with Einstein, not under him.

fields.what: Develops part of the information system, in collaboration with the solution architecture design.
fields.pollux: Babbage builds the exposure data engine feeding every portal view.

fields.what: Tests developments; testing the software is part of the responsibilities of all Agile Team Members.
fields.who: Independent Tester only if the organisation requires one
fields.pollux: Each ATeM tests their own work; no separate ESM test team is assumed.

fields.what: Provides progress information to the Team Coordinator, who consolidates it into the Development Status Report.
fields.pollux: Progress reaches you through Lovelace, never directly from the developers.

fields.what: Decides the best way to do the work in each iteration — the self-organising team principle in practice.
fields.pollux: The team, not the PM, decides how the scenario overlay gets built.

fields.what: Communicates and collaborates with the rest of the Agile Project Core Team, face to face wherever possible.
fields.pollux: Daily Stand-up every morning keeps in-house and seconded members aligned.

fields.what: Encompasses architecture, analysis, design, programming, testing, planning and estimation; specialisation depth varies per person.
fields.pollux: Lamarr is the developer but sizes, tests and designs alongside the rest.

fields.what: Whatever their background and experience, ATeMs collaborate with the rest of the team in a skill-growing environment.
fields.pollux: Eiffel's contract discipline about 'done' spreads to the in-house members.

fields.what: Drafts the Test Plan and provides technical advice on testing scope, types and techniques.
fields.who: PM accountable; TeCo, ArOw, PrOw support
fields.pollux: The ATeMs draft it; you stay accountable for the testing approach.

fields.what: Responsible and Accountable for the Daily Stand-up; ATeMs alone arrange the 'meet after' the TeCo noted.
fields.who: TeCo facilitates; PM and PrOw informed
fields.pollux: Conflict 4 — the stand-up is theirs, not the PM's status slot.

fields.what: Responsible for the setup and execution of the Review; may deliver the demo or delegate it to the Product Owner.
fields.who: PrOw accountable for the output; BM and BIG consulted
fields.pollux: Demonstrates the read-only exposure view before Release 1 on 29 Mar 2029.

fields.what: Responsible for all retrospective activities including collecting hard data and defining action plans; accountable for its outputs.
fields.who: TeCo facilitates; PrOw and BM informed if necessary
fields.pollux: Conflict 7 — the team must keep review and retrospective separate.

fields.what: Business analysts and similar experts may be invited temporarily to help the team understand context and scope.
fields.who: Invited alongside the PrOw, who remains the single voice
fields.pollux: A quarter-end analyst joins to explain the eleven-spreadsheet chain.

fields.what: Specialists in architecture, UX, security or database administration join temporarily to overcome specific technical challenges.
fields.pollux: Turing (LISO) advises on securing national-authority access for Release 3.

fields.what: Some organisations require a quality assurance team working in parallel to validate the software; the A-PCT still owns quality.
fields.who: Parallel QA team, if the organisation requires it
fields.pollux: If ESM requires parallel validation, it does not relieve the ATeMs.

traps: ATeMs are generalists — analysts and testers are ATeMs, not separate roles.
Testing belongs to every ATeM; an Independent Tester is optional and additional.
ATeMs report progress to the Team Coordinator, not to the Project Manager.
The ArOw, and the PM in ceremonies, act as regular Agile Team Members.
Domain and Technical Experts join temporarily; they are not A-PCT core roles.
